project.name: Great Easton Townscape Guide
project.boundarySource: ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024) with curated adjoining public green spaces
project.researchNotes: Townscape Guides batch audit completed 2026-08-11. Historic England and current public OpenStreetMap records were filtered point-in-polygon. The original settlement boundary is preserved in townStudyArea; 1 directly adjoining public green-space geometries were included in the active visitor boundary. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-11: 43 of 46 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown.

touristAppeal.label: Not a tourist town
touristAppeal.summary: Great Easton has recorded local interest, but its current in-boundary visitor offer does not meet the threshold for a tourist-town rating.

townGuide.headline: A practical local guide to Great Easton
townGuide.intro: Great Easton has a modest visitor offer within its active settlement boundary. The guide records defensible heritage and practical stops without presenting the place as a destination.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: CHURCH OF ST ANDREW
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start with CHURCH OF ST ANDREW, then use the planner for an in-boundary daytime stop.

townGuide.suggestedTime: As part of a wider local journey
townGuide.visitorMood: A local settlement rather than a tourist destination.

visitorHighlights.name: CHURCH OF ST ANDREW
visitorHighlights.reason: CHURCH OF ST ANDREW is a nationally recorded historic landmark within Great Easton. Access should be checked where it is not a public church or outdoor monument.

attractionGuide.headline: church
attractionGuide.intro: CHURCH OF ST ANDREW is a nationally recorded historic landmark within Great Easton. Access should be checked where it is not a public church or outdoor monument.

townStudyArea.sourceName: ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024) with curated adjoining public green spaces
